test_case.test_name: Parameterized CPU last-level-cache identity and sharing-topology validation
test_case.purpose: Verify each installed CPU exposes the approved last-level cache level, size, instances and socket/core sharing topology.
required_package: CPU/board/BIOS identity and operator installation record
Approved LLC definition: level/type, per-instance versus aggregate size, count and sharing topology
Required BIOS/Windows/Linux evidence and virtualization policy
Secure Linux access with lscpu and cache sysfs visibility
test_case.test_command: Operator captures CPU installation, BIOS and required Windows recognition. On Linux, securely collect full `lscpu`, `lscpu -C` and `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cache/index*/` level/type/size/id/ways/coherency_line_size/shared_cpu_list; correlate instances to sockets/NUMA/CPU model and compare only against the approved LLC definition.
test_case.expected_result: All installed CPUs report the expected LLC level, per-instance/aggregate size, instance count and sharing association with no missing/asymmetric cache or platform error.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires model-matched LLC interpretation and complete raw topology. Generic CPU recognition or an unqualified aggregate lscpu value cannot pass.
safety_gate: Physical CPU/cooling installation and power remain operator-only.
Detect virtualization or offline CPUs before interpreting topology.
Abort collection on hardware/SEL/thermal instability; do not auto-retry.
expected_evidence: CPU/socket/board/BIOS identity and manual install record
Approved LLC model comparison plus system logs
test_case.recovery: If topology is asymmetric or a cache index disappears, preserve per-CPU sysfs and online/offline state, make no firmware or CPU-affinity changes, return any approved temporary CPU-online state to baseline, and escalate socket/BIOS/virtualization interpretation to the processor owner.
